title: Response-filter lookup is keyed on the endpoint function, and the job filter depends on the creator wire field
answers: why is my POST route not filtered by the response filter
job search filter returns nothing for non-admins after changing the Job model
how do response filters find which route to filter
creator field missing from job JSON breaks ownership filtering
body:
Invariant: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_find_fastapi_response_filter takes only the request and looks up scope['endpoint'] in FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_RESPONSE_FILTERS. It no longer checks the HTTP method, so a POST collection route registered there is filtered too; the lookup is exact per function, so other routes get no filter.
_filter_search_jobs reads job['creator'] from the serialized JSON. That key exists only because mlflow/server/job_api.py:Job declares creator and from_job_entity copies job.creator. Renaming or dropping either silently hides every job from non-admins (fail-closed) rather than erroring.
Tests that compare the full job JSON, such as test_job_submit and test_job_cancel in tests/server/jobs/test_endpoint.py, must include "creator": None, since pydantic serializes unset optional fields as null (as with status_details).
Applies: any change to the Job response model or to response filter registration for job routes.
applies: Changes to job_api.Job, the response filter map, or job route serialization.
says: Job list appears completely empty for non-admin users after recent updates.
Non-administrators cannot see their submitted jobs in the jobs dashboard.
Restore ownership visibility so team members can view jobs they created.
Search jobs table returns zero results when logged in without administrator privileges.
search: Response filtering in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_find_fastapi_response_filter matches scope['endpoint'] against FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_RESPONSE_FILTERS without checking HTTP methods. Ownership filtering in _filter_search_jobs relies on the creator field serialized in mlflow/server/job_api.py:Job; omitting or renaming it silently hides all jobs from non-admin users. Tests comparing serialized job JSON, such as test_job_submit and test_job_cancel in tests/server/jobs/test_endpoint.py, must expect creator as None for unset optional fields. Applies to modifications of the Job response model, response filter registration, or job route serialization.
